# Inspect Practice — Full Content Corpus
> Comprehensive Transport Canada AME (Aircraft Maintenance Engineer) exam preparation platform.
> Covers TP14038E + License M (Airframe & Powerplant), E (Electronics), S (Structures).

## Platform Overview

Inspect Practice is an AI-powered exam preparation platform for aspiring Aircraft Maintenance Engineers in Canada. The platform provides 2,500+ practice questions covering the full Transport Canada AME curriculum, adaptive difficulty, timed simulation exams, AI tutor explanations, and detailed progress tracking.

### Features
- 2,500+ AME practice questions covering all Transport Canada standards (TP14038E)
- Adaptive difficulty that adjusts to your performance based on weak areas
- Timed simulation exams that mirror the actual Transport Canada licensing test
- AI Tutor with instant explanations for every question
- Detailed progress tracking and weak area identification by category
- Bilingual platform (English and French)
- Mobile-responsive web app — works on any device, no app download

## License Categories

### License M — Maintenance (Airframe & Powerplant)
- Covers airframe structures, systems, powerplant theory, and maintenance practices
- Most common AME category
- Requires 48 months of apprenticeship
- Focus: engines, hydraulics, landing gear, flight controls, propellers

### License E — Electronics (Avionics)
- Covers aircraft electrical systems, instruments, navigation systems, and communication equipment
- Requires 36 months of apprenticeship (with approved training)
- Focus: avionics, wiring, circuit analysis, radio systems, radar

### License S — Structures
- Covers sheet metal, composites, welding, NDT, and structural repairs
- Requires 36 months of apprenticeship (with approved training)
- Focus: structural analysis, materials, corrosion control, bonding

## Key Facts

### CARS Exam (Canadian Aviation Regulations)
- 100-150 multiple-choice questions
- Passing grade: 60%
- Covers: general provisions, aircraft maintenance standards, airworthiness, certification, safety management
- Part of Transport Canada TP14038E standard

### Salary Information
- Entry-level AME: $45,000–$60,000 CAD/year
- Mid-career: $60,000–$80,000 CAD/year
- Senior AME (with multiple ratings): $80,000–$100,000+ CAD/year
- Top-earning sectors: airlines, MRO facilities, helicopter operations

### Canadian Employment
- Over 50,000 AMEs employed across Canada
- Key employers: Air Canada, WestJet, Bombardier, CAE, field maintenance operators
- Growing demand due to retirements and fleet expansion

## How to Get Your AME License (6 Steps)
1. Choose your category: M (Airframe & Powerplant), E (Electronics), or S (Structures)
2. Complete Transport Canada-approved training at an accredited school
3. Study with Inspect Practice to identify weak areas and build confidence
4. Pass the CARS exam (Canadian Aviation Regulations) with 60%+
5. Pass your category-specific technical exam
6. Complete required apprenticeship hours and apply to Transport Canada

## FAQ

### How do I start studying for the AME exam?
Sign up for Inspect Practice — free tier provides access to one full category with practice questions. Use the AI tutor for instant explanations on any question you struggle with.

### What is TP14038E?
TP14038E is Transport Canada's standard publication for AME exam requirements. It defines the regulatory knowledge (CARS) and technical knowledge required for each license category.

### How long is the AME exam?
The CARS exam is typically 2-3 hours for 100-150 questions. Category technical exams vary by discipline.

### Can I retake the AME exam if I fail?
Yes. Transport Canada allows exam retakes. Inspect Practice helps you focus on your exact weak areas to improve your score before your next attempt.

### Do I need to go to school to become an AME?
You can either complete an approved training program (18-24 months) or work through a 48-month apprenticeship. Many successful AMEs combine both paths.
